# Support matrix

The aim is one behaviour in every language: each implementation of Bead plays the same conformance
files and is proven against the others in the interop. A difference stays on this page only until it
closes. The Rust side has its core
([0044](decisions/0044-rust-one-owner-per-router-traits-no-unsafe-two-parameters-no-warning.md)),
its transports over WebSocket and HTTP
([0049](decisions/0049-the-rust-sides-sockets-are-features-of-its-core-and-a-target-is-read-as-a-pages-browser-writes-it.md)),
its MQTT 5 binding, a client of its own over them
([0050](decisions/0050-the-rust-sides-broker-bindings-are-features-of-its-core-and-mqtt-5-a-client-of-its-own-over-its-sockets.md)),
and beadc's Rust target
([0051](decisions/0051-beadc-writes-rust-each-packages-typed-shells-beside-the-messages-buffa-writes.md)),
each part it lacks a row of the [differences](#differences) ahead, and plays the parts of the files
it reaches: each part of them it does not play is held to its row, of kind open, by
`spec/check.py`'s `AHEAD` ([0004](decisions/0004-one-behaviour-in-every-language.md)), and the stage
that brings it deletes that row.

Every cell is read from the tests. A cell that names a test file is supported, and that file, with the `describe` (TypeScript), the test class or method (C#) or the test function or trial (Rust) named beside it, proves it. Each name is copied from its test to the byte, `…` standing for any run of it, and the parentheses after a file hold the names its tests declare, or the entries and cases they play, and nothing else; `tools/check-citations.mjs` holds every citation of this page, wherever it stands. "Not tested" means no test holds it, whatever the code does; "not available" means the implementation has no such part. TypeScript test paths are under `implementations/typescript/src/`, C# test paths under `implementations/dotnet/tests/`, Rust test paths under `implementations/rust/crates/`, but those written from the repository's root. The sections of `spec/spec.md` say what each feature is, and those of its companion `spec/debugging.md`, cited as "debugging §", what a side traces, filters and counts beside the wire, and those of `spec/transcoding.md`, cited as "transcoding §", what a side's gateway answers over HTTP; [the decisions](decisions/README.md) say why it is so.

The TypeScript side's unit tests run under Node alone, in one Playwright project and no browser: the Web Worker transport is tested over a `MessageChannel`, and the clients over Node's `WebSocket`, `ws` and `fetch`. One client runs in a browser: the HTTP client, bundled into a page Chromium loads from another origin than the interop service's HTTP server it calls on each side, and into a page whose own server answers its connect with a redirect, by `implementations/typescript/browser/__tests__/cors-page.test.ts` under `playwright.browser.config.ts` (`yarn test:browser`).

Over a broker, every side does the same, the Rust side's core over its in-memory broker and over
MQTT 5 among them, and what that costs is stated in its records
([0038](decisions/0038-over-a-broker-a-connection-is-placed-once-at-its-open-named-by-both-its-ends.md)):
calls spread across a name's participants by connection, not by call; a participant added takes no
connection already placed, and one stopped ends every connection of its own; and each participant
needs a broker identity of its own. Ahead, on every side: a connection's age and a graceful drain,
for every long-lived transport at once, a WebSocket's and a broker's, as HTTP/2's `GOAWAY` drains
one ([RFC 9113 §6.8](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113#section-6.8)) and gRPC's
`MAX_CONNECTION_AGE` re-spreads them; what
[0040](decisions/0040-a-brokers-adapter-offers-bytes-at-topics-and-bead-keeps-its-own-credit-credential-and-heartbeat.md)
keeps ahead of a broker: an acceptor that proves itself to its opener, and a publisher's identity a
broker vouches for standing for an `ELSEWHERE`, RabbitMQ's validated `user-id` its way over AMQP 1.0
([0043](decisions/0043-over-amqp-1-0-a-participant-is-one-connection-whose-exclusive-inbox-ends-with-it-and-a-parcel-one-message-of-one-profile-each-counted-to-its-byte.md));
a relay that carries a subscription, which a page across a broker needs
([0019](decisions/0019-a-relay-terminates-each-leg-and-routes-nothing-past-it.md)); and what
[0041](decisions/0041-over-mqtt-5-a-participant-is-one-clean-link-and-a-parcel-one-publish-each-counted-to-its-byte.md)
keeps ahead over MQTT 5: an Authentication Method, MQTT 5's enhanced authentication
([§4.12](https://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v5.0/os/mqtt-v5.0-os.html)), and EMQX played beside
Mosquitto; Mosquitto under TLS played, a client certificate among it, where the row of MQTT 5 over
TLS above holds "not tested".

MQTT 5 is a broker's first binding, on every side, the Rust side's a client of its own over its
core's sockets
([0050](decisions/0050-the-rust-sides-broker-bindings-are-features-of-its-core-and-mqtt-5-a-client-of-its-own-over-its-sockets.md)),
and what it costs is stated in its record
([0041](decisions/0041-over-mqtt-5-a-participant-is-one-clean-link-and-a-parcel-one-publish-each-counted-to-its-byte.md)):
every case of the in-memory broker that a real broker can play plays against the Mosquitto 2.1.2
`tools/mqtt-broker.mjs` starts, which each side's suite skips, saying so, where no broker is
given, and which CI's job `mqtt` requires. A deployment's access control grants a name on its own
topic, and one that denies a server's participant leaves its clients' connects to time out; a
participant's link carries its broker's Receive Maximum a round trip; a link taken over is fenced,
and its participant connects no more until it is started again; and Mosquitto 2.1.2 counts a
Remaining Length as one byte toward a subscriber and as none from a publisher, which Bead's own
count never reaches. Its WebSocket listener takes no fragmented message, so every side sends each as
one frame, a row of [Leveled down](#leveled-down).

AMQP 1.0 on RabbitMQ 4 is a broker's second binding, the TypeScript and C# sides alike, the Rust
side's ahead with `Rust's AMQP 1.0 binding`, and what it costs is stated in its record
([0043](decisions/0043-over-amqp-1-0-a-participant-is-one-connection-whose-exclusive-inbox-ends-with-it-and-a-parcel-one-message-of-one-profile-each-counted-to-its-byte.md)):
every case of the in-memory broker that a real broker can play but the will's and the takeover's
plays against the RabbitMQ 4.4.0 `tools/amqp-broker.mjs` starts, which each of their suites skips,
saying so, where no broker is given, and which CI's job `amqp` requires. The C# side's bytes are
AMQPNetLite 2.5.5's, which takes no message already written, held to the profile by `amqpMessages`,
which fails on the day an upgrade writes another encoding; the TypeScript side writes the profile
itself and hands rhea 3.0.5 its bytes. A participant is one connection, its inbox exclusive to it; a
name its broker denies ends its own session alone; no receiver names a max-message-size; and the
publisher's identity a broker vouches for is ahead, RabbitMQ's validated `user-id` its way over AMQP
1.0. Each part that parts it from MQTT 5 is a row of Differences, its kind the standard's or the
platform's.

## Interop

Each client of the TypeScript and C# sides is played against the other's server of the interop
service (`spec/interop-blueprint.json` and `spec/interop-service.json`), over each transport both
serve, and each one's generated HTTP client against the gateway the other's interop server serves
beside it, of `spec/transcoding.proto`'s service. The Rust side's client is played against the
TypeScript and C# servers, and their clients against its server, `bead-interop-server`, over
WebSocket, HTTP/1.1 and MQTT 5; its AMQP 1.0 binding and its gateway are ahead.

The cases are the same on every side: a payload echoed, and a value outside ASCII
echoed equal with its members in another order, a string of the length asked, the application's own
failure, an unknown procedure and service, an admission that refuses, a resolver that throws, a
payload that is not JSON, a request its rules refuse, answered `PAYLOAD_INVALID` with its
violations, and one they take, a call cancelled by its signal and one past its timeout (each
cancelled at the server too), a command the server asks, an unpaced subscription and a paced one, a
session opened and ended, a call presenting the session it learned, a `JWT` presented by default and
run in its credential's session, an `ELSEWHERE` carried in each `POST`'s `Authorization` over HTTP
and in its upgrade's over a WebSocket, durations held as section 1.4 holds them, and, over WebSocket
alone, 3 MiB each way as transfers. The TypeScript side counts more tests than cases, as it splits
the echo from the bytes, and the refusals, into tests of their own where the C# side gathers them in
theories; the Rust side plays them as the TypeScript side splits them, a trial a case, a transport
and a server, its own server's among them. Over HTTP, each side's client sends each envelope in an
exchange of its own, in no guaranteed order (spec 15.5), so each side's interop tests keep a call's
envelopes in order by a guard of their own, the TypeScript side's `fetchInOrder`, the C# side's
`InOrder` and the Rust side's `InOrder`, which lets one go once the server answered the head of the
one before. Over the other side's gateway, each generated HTTP client calls with protobuf's JSON and
every native encoding, reads its problems and presents its authorization, reads a stream's result,
its notifications and the failure that ends it, and the gateway's own refusals of a route, a size
and a busy stream, and compares the two gateways' OpenAPI documents byte for byte: five tests a
side, each twin named by the same sentence.

The conversations and the transports' cases hold a server to them, and over a broker a client's
transport too, by the client role of the transports' file. A client's behaviour over HTTP and a
WebSocket is held to the other sides by the interop alone, but for what it holds of a duration it is
given, which the durations' file holds; a client part of the transports' file for them, ahead,
holds it by a decision of its own.

What no entry plays stays with each side's twin tests, which name each unit they hold by its own
number, `spec 15.10` or `debugging 4.2`, in a test's title or a comment just above its declaration,
where `spec/units.txt` or `spec/debugging-units.txt` gives it `twins`, and `spec/check.py` holds
that a test of each side does:

- what a writer refuses and what a client alone does, which the conversations, playing a server,
  cannot reach: what a writer never writes (spec 4.10), `router/shared/__tests__/header.test.ts`
  (`writeHeader`, its `refuses …` tests) and
  `Bead.Core.Tests/EnvelopeCodecHeaderTests.Refuses_to_write_a_header_and_writes_nothing`; a
  failure's detail as a writer cuts it (spec 7.4), `envelope.test.ts` (`writeFailure`) and
  `EnvelopeCodecTests` (`Cuts_the_detail_at_the_limit_at_a_character_s_boundary`,
  `Writes_a_lone_surrogate_as_U_FFFD`); a code's block and a code no name gives,
  kept as its number (spec 8.1), `constants.test.ts` (`ProtocolCode`) and `errors.test.ts`
  (`FailureError`), and `FailureExceptionTests.Keeps_a_protocol_code_no_name_has_as_a_number`;
  the reservation made with the cancel (spec 10.4), `router-requester.test.ts`
  (`cancel a call still waiting once: rejected, told, and its call id reserved on its connection alone`)

## An example's halves

`examples/hello` is a project written as a consumer writes one
([0022](decisions/0022-a-proto-becomes-one-checked-blueprint-and-each-language-is-generated-from-it.md)):
its TypeScript, C# and Rust halves, each built with its messages generated by beadc and by its
platform's own generator. The C# half's external build compiles Grpc.Tools' messages, from its own
protoc, under beadc's service code; the TypeScript half's runs protoc-gen-es under `buf generate`
at the pin beadc runs, so it proves the project's own generation and `messagesOut`'s import, not
another generator's output; the Rust half's runs `bead_protobuf_build::config_of` in its build
script over the set `buf build` writes, Buffa's own generator, the feature `external` choosing the
mount
([0051](decisions/0051-beadc-writes-rust-each-packages-typed-shells-beside-the-messages-buffa-writes.md)).
Each client calls each server over WebSocket and writes
[`transcript.txt`](../examples/hello/transcript.txt), then the TypeScript and C# servers' gateway
answers what a person asks it with curl over HTTP/1.1, through the in-memory transport joined to
its WebSocket one: CI's `examples` job, through `examples/hello/pairs.mjs`. What a consumer of the
TypeScript runtime's sources must set, which the C# half never meets, is a row of the
[differences](#differences).

| Client               | Server               | Messages                | Transport                    | Pairs | Test                                                                          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript, C#, Rust | TypeScript, C#, Rust | beadc's, the platform's | WebSocket                    |    36 | `examples/hello/pairs.mjs`                                                    |
| curl's requests      | TypeScript, C#       | beadc's, the platform's | HTTP/1.1, the gateway        |    24 | `examples/hello/pairs.mjs`, the gateway's lines of `transcript.txt`           |
| curl's requests      | Rust                 | beadc's, the platform's | HTTP/1.1, the gateway        |     0 | ahead: `Rust's gateway`                                                       |
| either               | either               | either                  | HTTP/1.1, the HTTP transport |     0 | not run: the interop holds HTTP; the example serves Bead over WebSocket alone |

## beadc's wrappers

A project runs beadc's image through two wrappers it commits, `beadc.sh` under bash and `beadc.ps1`
under PowerShell
([0022](decisions/0022-a-proto-becomes-one-checked-blueprint-and-each-language-is-generated-from-it.md)).
They are one contract: each case of `builder/src/__tests__/wrappers.test.ts` runs both, `beadc.ps1`
by `pwsh -File` and inside a session, against a stand-in engine that records each call, and holds
them to one engine call, one output and one exit, so a difference between them is a red test. Its
cases run on every leg of CI's `builder` job, on Linux, amd64 and arm64, and on Windows. What one
shell cannot do is a row of a kind the [differences](#differences) define, with the test that shows
it.

| Behaviour                                                | Kind     | `beadc.sh`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `beadc.ps1`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The shell that runs it                                   | platform | bash 3.2 or later; `sh`, where it is not bash, refused, exit 3: `wrappers.test.ts` (`each wrapper refuses the shell it is not written for, exit 3`)                                                                                                                                                              | PowerShell 7.6 or later; Windows PowerShell 5.1, which drops an empty argument and a quote from a native command's arguments and splits the mount's path at a space, refused, exit 3, where its execution policy lets the file load: the same test, under `Bypass`; 7.4 and 7.5, out of support from 10 Nov 2026, refused, exit 3, by the same check, which no runner's pwsh, 7.6.6, reaches                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| One engine call, one output and one exit for one call    | —        | `wrappers.test.ts` (`each wrapper makes the same engine calls, prints the same bytes and exits alike: …`), its cases on Linux and on Windows, each host's links among them, junctions on Windows                                                                                                                 | the same test, each case by `pwsh -File` and inside a session                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| An execution policy that refuses the file, on Windows    | platform | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | PowerShell's exit 1 and its message, before a line of the wrapper runs: Windows PowerShell's `Restricted`, the Windows client's default, a group policy's `AllSigned`, `RemoteSigned` on a file marked as downloaded; `pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./beadc.ps1` runs it: `wrappers.test.ts` (`an execution policy that refuses beadc.ps1 stops PowerShell before its first line, exit 1`), `pwsh` under `AllSigned` and `powershell` under `Restricted`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A redirect inside a session on Windows                   | platform | the engine's bytes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | the engine's characters, UTF-8, each line ended CRLF by PowerShell's `>` and `2>`; by `pwsh -File`, the engine's bytes: `wrappers.test.ts` (`in a session, beadc.ps1 passes the engine's UTF-8 whole, and a > on Windows writes its lines CRLF`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A bare `--`                                              | platform | passed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | passed by `pwsh -File`; taken by PowerShell inside a session, and `'--'`, quoted, passed: `wrappers.test.ts` (`in a session, a bare -- does not reach the engine, and a quoted '--' does`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Differences

A difference is of one of three kinds. **Platform**: a platform imposes it, and it stays while the platform does. **Standard**: a binding's standard parts it from another binding's, every side alike, and it stays while the standards do. **Open**: nothing imposes it, and closing it is work to do.

## Leveled down

A leveling is no difference, since every side behaves alike: it is a place where Bead does less than a standard, or its own wire, allows, because one platform cannot do more and every side keeps to what it can ([0004](decisions/0004-one-behaviour-in-every-language.md)). Each is kept here with what would lift it, so that it can be lifted, on every side at once, once the platform can.
